cobol_source:
*================================================================*
      * PROGRAM : HIGHPAID                                             *
      * PURPOSE : EXTRACT EMPLOYEES EARNING ABOVE A THRESHOLD (60,000) *
      * INPUT   : data/input/employees.dat                             *
      * OUTPUT  : data/output/high_earners.dat                         *
      *================================================================*
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. HIGHPAID.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT EMP-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/input/employees.dat"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
           SELECT OUT-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/output/high_earners.dat"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD  EMP-FILE.
           COPY EMPREC.
       FD  OUT-FILE.
       01  OUT-RECORD              PIC X(54).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-EOF                  PIC X VALUE 'N'.
           88  END-OF-FILE         VALUE 'Y'.
       01  WS-THRESHOLD            PIC 9(07)V99 VALUE 60000.00.
       01  WS-READ                 PIC 9(03) VALUE 0.
       01  WS-SELECTED             PIC 9(03) VALUE 0.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           OPEN INPUT EMP-FILE OUTPUT OUT-FILE
           PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               READ EMP-FILE
                   AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
                   NOT AT END
                       ADD 1 TO WS-READ
                       IF EMP-SALARY > WS-THRESHOLD
                           ADD 1 TO WS-SELECTED
                           WRITE OUT-RECORD FROM EMP-RECORD
                       END-IF
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM
           CLOSE EMP-FILE OUT-FILE
           DISPLAY "HIGHPAID: " WS-SELECTED " OF " WS-READ
                   " RECORDS SELECTED"
           STOP RUN.

plan.approach: The COBOL program is a sequential-file batch extract: read every record from EMP-FILE, increment WS-READ for each, write those whose EMP-SALARY strictly exceeds the 60 000.00 threshold to OUT-FILE, increment WS-SELECTED, then print summary counters. The modernization maps each paragraph and working-storage variable 1-to-1 into a Spring Boot service method (HighPaidService.execute()), keeping the counter variables (wsRead, wsSelected), the threshold (HighpaidProperties.salaryThreshold = 60000.00), and the strict-greater-than comparison identical. The flat output file is still produced (mirroring OUT-FILE) while results are also persisted to a PostgreSQL table. Flyway manages schema lifecycle; an ApplicationRunner replaces the JCL/batch entry point; a REST controller allows on-demand triggering.
patterns_used: Repository Pattern (Spring Data JPA) – EmployeeRepository / HighEarnerRepository
Service Layer – HighPaidService encapsulates all MAIN-PARA business logic
Configuration Properties – HighpaidProperties externalises WS-THRESHOLD and OUT-FILE path
ApplicationRunner – replaces JCL/batch scheduler entry point
Streaming cursor (Stream<Employee>) – mirrors sequential PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE read loop without loading all rows into memory
Flyway database migrations – version-controlled schema equivalent of copybook / DDL
REST Controller – on-demand HTTP trigger for the batch
Try-with-resources – guarantees file and DB cursor close (CLOSE EMP-FILE OUT-FILE)
Value Object (BatchResult) – immutable carrier for WS-READ / WS-SELECTED counters
Testcontainers integration test – validates business logic against a real PostgreSQL instance
plan.sql_strategy: There are no EXEC SQL blocks in the original COBOL; data came from a flat file (EMP-FILE). In the modernized version the flat file is replaced by the employees PostgreSQL table. EmployeeRepository.streamAllOrderByEmpId() opens a server-side cursor (via Spring Data JPA @Query + Stream<T>) inside a single @Transactional context, faithfully reproducing the sequential read. Inserts to high_earners use HighEarnerRepository.save() with JPA batch-insert tuning (jdbc.batch_size=50). The strict > comparison (COBOL IF EMP-SALARY > WS-THRESHOLD) is reproduced as BigDecimal.compareTo(threshold) > 0 to avoid floating-point rounding.
plan.call_strategy: The original COBOL program contains no CALL statements. External dependencies (file I/O and display) are handled by Java's NIO BufferedWriter (flat file) and SLF4J logger (DISPLAY statement) respectively. No service proxies or adapters were needed.
